findings.defect: Every whitecap within about 30 m of a 2-3 m camera is a soft-edged, partly transparent white smear with no internal structure. In overcast.png it is a 30 x 18 px ellipse with a smooth fall-off and nothing inside; in the splashdown scene at 1440p it is a 300 px wide patch of airbrushed, cloud-like wisps with the wave shading showing through it. It reads as fog or a smudge lying on the water, in the foreground of the splashdown close-up. The first review's finding 8 (plastic foam) is still fully visible after the fix.
findings.realReference: Recovery-ship footage of a capsule in the water: foam is opaque white where a crest has just broken and breaks up into a sharp-edged lace of bubble rafts with dark holes, stretched along the wave's travel and thinning into a net of fine lines. Edges are crisp at pixel scale from 3 m; foam hides the specular highlights beneath it. It is never a Gaussian blob.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/ocean/shaders/surfaceWgsl.ts fragment lines 302-322. Coverage is the cascades' foam textures (written in fftWgsl.ts lines 184-189) sampled bilinearly: one texel is 4.6 m (cascade 0), 1.1 m (cascade 1), 0.28 m (cascade 2), so near the camera the mask is a magnified blur. The lace only gates it through smoothstep(th - hw, th + hw, laceN) with th clamped at OCEAN_FOAM_CORE 0.22 once foamJ > 0.68; laceN = 0.5 + 0.3 lace is almost always above that, so the core is uniformly white ('bubbles' only varies 0.8-1.0), and min(foamJ * 3, 1) turns the rim into a linear ramp of the blurred texture (the translucent halo). Foam also only mixes albedo in waterFoamCoverage / brdfWaterDirect (waterBrdf.ts lines 183-186, 329-332): the normal and roughness stay the water's, which is why waves shade through it.
findings.fixDirection: Use the low-resolution foam field as a DENSITY that drives a high-frequency, sea-anchored foam pattern: threshold a multi-octave bubble/cellular pattern (or the fine cascades' convergence at full amplitude) against the density so that coverage is binary at pixel scale and the density sets hole size, with a thresholded rim instead of a ramp. Give the whitecap cascades more foam resolution near the camera (a camera- or vessel-centred foam clipmap at 5 cm texels or finer), stretch foam along the local wave direction, and shade foam as a diffuse layer with its own normal and no water specular through it. Judge at 1440p from 3 m beside the capsule.

findings.defect: From 5 to 30 km the sea is a smooth blue-grey gradient with a blurry grey smudge where the glint should be. alt30k.png: the whole frame spans sRGB luminance 48-128, the glint peaks at 128 (mid-grey) and its only structure is isotropic noise blotches 40-80 px across plus one bright blob with a hard outline at (690,555). climb-16389m.png is a gradient and a smudge and nothing else. alt10k.png / handover-near-on.png / perf-10km-1440p.png: the lower half of the frame carries fine wave texture and the upper half carries none; the texture stops along an arc (the screen centre of alt10k is 15.5 km away, exactly fadeStart), so a disc of textured water sits on a blurred sheet. Energy across the hand-over is fine (near field on vs off differs by 0.3/255 on average); it is the look that changes.
findings.realReference: From an airliner or a balloon over open ocean: saturated dark-blue water, a glint several times brighter than the sea around it (about 5-9 x at 7 m/s wind) with a crisp fine-grained sparkle texture that continues to the horizon, wind streaks and slick bands aligned with the wind, long swell lines, haze only in the last degrees before the horizon. Texture never stops at a fixed radius under the aircraft.
findings.likelyCause: (1) The far sheet is shaded without any wave structure: all resolved slopes fade out between detailFadeFraction x fadeStart (10.5 km) and fadeStart 15 km (oceanDetail in src/render/ocean/shaders/waves.ts line 216; data/defs/render/earth.ocean.json nearFieldFadeStartM, detailFadeFraction), and beyond it the deferred sheet only has WATER_FIELD_WGSL (src/render/ocean/shaders/waterBrdf.ts lines 84-117): isotropic gradient-noise octaves with exp(0.3-0.35 x noise) amplitude, i.e. about +-35 %, whose 1.4:1 downwind stretch is invisible. (2) labs/ocean/labSky.ts in-scatter plus the fixed EV 15 of the altitude presets (labs/ocean/main.ts PRESETS) flatten the contrast: glint to sea is 2.8 x in linear terms in alt30k. (3) One wind speed (7 m/s) everywhere gives a broad Cox-Munk lobe whose peak is about mid-grey at EV 15. The integrated shots out/screens/integration/water-climb-all-14km.png (taken before the fix round) show the same gradient with a featureless grey glint column under the real atmosphere, so the lab sky is not the whole cause.
findings.fixDirection: Keep wave-scale structure in the far sheet's shading: sample a filtered slope-moment representation (mean slope plus variance, LEAN/LEADR style) of the long-wave layer and swell in brdf_water for the deferred path, so the glint's texture continues past fadeStart and fades by pixel footprint, not by distance from the camera. Make the roughness field strongly anisotropic (wind rows and slick bands 5-10:1 along the wind, with sharp fronts) and give it a real dynamic range (slope variance from about 0.008 in calm bands to 0.05). Replace or bound the lab sky's in-scatter, expose by meter in the lab, and re-shoot 3, 10, 16 and 30 km in the integrated app.

findings.defect: The orbital sun glint is a dim grey disc on a dark-blue gradient: peak sRGB luminance 101 of 255, no highlight, and its internal structure is half a dozen soft bone-shaped blobs (smoothstepped noise) that read as fog wisps. Position and width pass the spec; the picture does not read as sunlight on water.
findings.realReference: ISS photographs of sunglint: silver-white to golden, saturating at the specular point, with a filigree of dark and bright streaks inside it (slicks, internal waves, ship wakes, wind shadows behind islands), a 10:1 range within the glint and sharp edges where calm water meets roughened water.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/ocean/shaders/waterBrdf.ts lines 92-116: wind = two noise octaves with log amplitude 0.35, slick = smoothstep(0.15, 0.6, noise) x calm with depth 0.35, so the lobe's variance changes by about +-40 % and only in a few rounded patches. With U10 = 7 m/s everywhere the peak radiance is E F / (4 pi sigma^2 cos) = about 4.5 kcd/m2, mid-grey at the lab's EV 15 (labs/ocean/main.ts preset leo), dimmer than a sunlit cloud by 5 x.
findings.fixDirection: Let the slope variance vary over at least a decade across the visible disc (calm pools to trade-wind seas) with streak-like, wind-aligned structure from 1 to 50 km and sharp fronts; keep the area mean at Cox-Munk so the width check still holds. Expose the lab view by meter, and verify in the integrated app that the core of the glint clips and feeds bloom.

findings.view: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\ocean\alt500.png (x 470-830, y 430-670); alt3k.png; night.png (moon path, x 450-850, y 330-650); markers-with-chop.png (lower half); midday.png (x 380-900, y 540-720); climb-273m.png
findings.defect: The glint is a flat matt grey plate crossed by dark vein lines 1-2 px wide, like cracked plaster or crumpled foil, with isolated single dark pixels inside it: 43 in alt500, 23 in alt3k, 28 in markers-with-chop, 14 in midday, 310 in the moon path of night.png, each under 45 % of its 5x5 median (down to 3 %), all exactly one pixel. Near the camera the highlights are soft pale blobs, not sparkles. No sun-glitter pixel clips: midday at 2 m has maximum 249 and 99.9th percentile 204; alt500 has maximum 185. The single dark pixels will flicker in motion (the integrated shot out/screens/integration/budget-splashdown.png shows the same thing as isolated saturated-blue pixels).
findings.realReference: Sun glitter is thousands of discrete images of the sun: pixel-sharp, saturated (2 % of 1.6e9 cd/m2 clips at any exposure), their density following the wave slopes. From 500 m it is a fine sparkling grain with brighter and dimmer bands along the waves and no dark cracks; a moon path is made of short horizontal dashes.
findings.likelyCause: (a) src/render/ocean/shaders/surfaceWgsl.ts line 371: grad = ... e * (sx / max(jxx, 0.25)) + f * (sy / max(jyy, 0.25)). The per-axis division by the cascade Jacobian multiplies ALL summed slopes by up to 4 along pinched crests, including the capillary layers (lines 325-343) and the long-wave layer (lines 347-366) that were never displaced by that Jacobian; the facet leaves the lobe in thin lines and single texels. (b) Everything below the pixel footprint is a smooth GGX lobe (waterAlpha in waterBrdf.ts lines 178-181; floor unresolvedSlopeVariance 0.0025 gives alpha >= 0.065, the sun smeared over +-3.7 deg), so each pixel shows the ensemble mean: correct energy, no sparkle statistics. (c) TAA averages what moves (taaReactive 0.45).
findings.fixDirection: Apply the Jacobian only to the cascades' own slopes, with the full 2x2 inverse, and soft-limit the final slope (about 0.6, the Stokes limit) so no facet spikes. Add a stochastic glint term for the unresolved variance (discrete microfacet counts per pixel footprint on a sea-anchored hash, in the manner of Chermain et al. or Zirr and Kaplanyan) so pixels scatter around the Cox-Munk mean and the bright ones clip into bloom; lower the variance floor within about 20 m of the camera. Add an assertion that counts single-pixel outliers inside the glint.

findings.defect: Seen from above, whitecaps are round blobs 2-3 m across and single-pixel specks scattered without orientation: a star field in the debug view, sprinkled salt in the shaded views. Coverage is calibrated (0.117 %), the shapes are not.
findings.realReference: At 7 m/s whitecaps are arcs along breaking crests, 3-10 m long and 0.5-2 m wide, all lying across the wind, each trailing a fading streak downwind; from 300-500 m they are short white dashes with one common orientation, often lined up in windrows.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/ocean/shaders/fftWgsl.ts line 187: fresh foam where a cascade's own Jacobian is more than foamSigma = 3.0 standard deviations below 1. Excursions of a near-isotropic Gaussian field at 3 sigma are compact, near-circular maxima, taken per cascade. Line 188 lets foam decay where it was born (no advection, no stretching), and where the cascades are filtered the statistical coverage arrives as isolated pixels (surfaceWgsl.ts line 322).
findings.fixDirection: Use a crest-following breaking criterion on the combined surface (swell plus all cascades) along the wind direction, with a lower threshold so the active region is a strip along the crest; advect the foam with the crest and stretch it downwind; decay in two stages (bright active foam, then a longer-lived residual streak). Keep the Monahan mean as the calibration target.

findings.defect: Looking down from 150 m to 3 km the surface is an isotropic bump field (blue sandpaper at 150 m, orange peel at 3 km): lumps 10-20 m across with no preferred direction, uniform from edge to edge. No crest lines of a wind sea, no direction a player could read the wind from.
findings.realReference: Aerial photographs of a 7 m/s sea: roughly parallel, short-crested crest lines 30-80 m apart, finer ripples lying across the wind, and from 3 km a clearly directional streaked texture.
findings.likelyCause: The drawn heights hold no wind sea: the spectrum is high-passed at 25 m (earth.ocean.json highPassWavelengthM) while the JONSWAP peak for U10 7 m/s and 200 km fetch is near 76 m. That energy exists only as the four swell sinusoids of data/defs/bodies/earth.json (request ocean-5, with the lead) and as the normals-only long-wave layer, drawn as two copies of one realisation rotated by -20 and +20 deg (longWaveSpreadDeg; surfaceWgsl.ts lines 347-366), which widens its spread; the cascades below 25 m have broad spreading by nature.
findings.fixDirection: Get ocean-5 answered (eight components with directional spread, or a physics-shared long-wave field). In the ocean's own paths: keep the long-wave layer's own directional spectrum (two independent realisations instead of rotated copies, or a rotation of a few degrees), raise its weight against the short chop in the shading, and compare 150 m, 500 m and 3 km shots with aerial photographs for readable wind direction.

findings.defect: A submerged object leaves a hard-edged stencil of its UNREFRACTED silhouette on the water. The yellow ball's refracted image is correctly lifted to y = 255, but at the straight-line position there is a 50 x 50 px oval with a 2 px step at its edge: green 18 % lower and red 11 % higher than the water beside it, and visibly rougher ripples inside. It looks like a flat decal floating over the shelf. (handover-refraction.png does not show it only because that shot is taken within a frame of re-adding the ball, see the last finding.)
findings.realReference: A submerged object seen through waves has one image, displaced and squashed toward the surface, with a wobbling, broken outline; the water surface above it looks like the water next to it.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/ocean/shaders/surfaceWgsl.ts: the pixel is classified by the G-buffer material straight behind it. Line 247 seabed = TERRAIN or REGOLITH; lines 253-257 leave seaDepth = OCEAN_DEEP for anything else; line 260 then gives full open-ocean cascade amplitudes (no TMA) and line 349 the full long-wave layer; line 416 sets s.albedo = 0 (imagery tint lost) and line 424 encodes 200 m depth. So inside the silhouette of any non-terrain object the water switches from shelf water to deep-ocean water, per pixel. The vertex stage does the same at lines 116-117 (oceanColumnDepthAt).
findings.fixDirection: An object in the water must not change the water's own properties. Take the water depth for TMA, shore foam and body colour from the seabed around or under the object (the vertical march skipping non-terrain fragments, a dilated or low-resolution seabed-depth buffer, or the smooth vertex-interpolated depth), never switch amplitudes on a per-pixel material test, and let the object contribute only through the refraction path. Add a spec that compares the unrefracted silhouette region with its surroundings after TAA has converged.

findings.view: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\ocean\refraction.png (x 660-1160, y 215-415); shore.png (x 420-920, y 300-420); handover-refraction.png; shoreAlong.png; overcast.png (x 640-1280, y 290-370)
findings.defect: Thin dark hairlines run along wave crests in the middle and far water, like scratches or wood grain. On the shelf they are near-black against turquoise: (44,60,68) against a median of (51,117,113) in refraction.png, (53,68,71) against (57,93,104) in shore.png, 1-2 px tall and tens of px long. Under overcast the far water looks like brushed wood.
findings.realReference: Wave faces turned toward the viewer are darker and more saturated than the sky-reflecting backs, but as broad soft bands that follow the wave, and steep crests over a bright bottom glow lighter green because light passes through them. Far water averages to a soft, slightly streaked texture.
findings.likelyCause: The same slope spikes as in the glint finding (surfaceWgsl.ts line 371) turn the shading normal toward the viewer in thin lines. There the refracted ray runs almost along the view ray, cosT is clamped to 0.15 (line 500), reach grows to 33-50 m (line 503) and the bed is seen through a 15-20 m water path (att at lines 559-564): the bottom contribution collapses to the column colour. There is no transmission term through thin crests.
findings.fixDirection: Limit the shading slope as in the glint finding; bound the in-water path used for attenuation by what the local depth and a physically possible refraction angle allow (the refracted ray cannot leave the Snell cone of the true surface), and filter the normal used for refraction with the pixel footprint. Consider a crest translucency term for steep faces over shallow, bright beds.

findings.view: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\ocean\shoreAlong.png (tan patch x 150-560, y 400-600, edge near (300,430)); perf-coast-1440p.png (x 480-1120, y 640-940 of 2560x1440)
findings.defect: Shallow water switches between two looks in patches that do not follow the seabed. I projected the lab's beachHeight into both cameras: the true depth grows monotonically away from the beach, yet shoreAlong shows textured green water close to the waterline (0.2-1.5 m) and a smooth tan patch farther out where the water is 1.5-3 m deep, with a crisp edge between them. From 60 m (perf-coast) the waterline is ringed by contour-like bands in the order tan, green, tan, turquoise. The swash foam is a flat white strip with stair-stepped edges. (The straight diagonal colour edge in perf-coast is the end of the lab's 900 m beach mesh, not an ocean fault.)
findings.realReference: Over a sloping sand bed the colour runs continuously from sand through pale green to turquoise as the depth grows, modulated only by real bars and by refraction caustics; the same depth has the same colour whichever way the camera looks.
findings.likelyCause: Two bottom estimates with different colours are blended by march confidence (surfaceWgsl.ts lines 540-564, conf = 1 - smoothstep(0.6, 1.0, tHit / reach)): the screen-space refracted bed (lit, textured sand through att(hitDepth)) and the modelled bottom (flat imagery albedo at seaDepth). The depths feeding them come from coarse marches: oceanDepthBelow (lines 81-107) uses 7 quadratically spaced steps, interpolates in eye distance (strongly non-linear at grazing angles) and falls back to alongRay, reach or 0 at different pixels; the refraction march has 6 steps with the last one covering 30 % of the reach. Which step the crossing falls in decides the look, hence contour-shaped patches.
findings.fixDirection: Make both estimates agree before blending them: light the modelled bottom like the bed (same albedo source and sun term) and use one depth for both. Refine the crossing by a few binary-search steps along the actual ray and interpolate in depth, not eye distance; remove the discontinuous fallbacks (alongRay / reach / 0). Add a spec that checks colour against true depth on the lab beach from two camera headings.

findings.view: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\ocean\splash.png (capsule at x 390-490, y 295-375); perf-splash-1440p.png (capsule at x 780-980, y 520-680 of 2560x1440)
findings.defect: The white capsule, the brightest object in the frame, has no effect on the water around it: no reflection under or in front of the hull, no darkening of the water where the hull hides the sky, no visible wet band at the waterline. It looks pasted onto the sea.
findings.realReference: Recovery footage of Crew Dragon and Orion: a broken, vertically smeared bright reflection of the hull lies on the water below it, the water beside the hull is darker where the hull blocks the sky, and the hull has a dark wet band above the waterline.
findings.likelyCause: waterSkyRadiance (src/render/ocean/shaders/waterBrdf.ts lines 267-317) samples only the environment probe or the sky-view table; the forward pass has 'scene.colorCopy' and 'scene.depthOpaque' bound but uses them for refraction only, and s.ao is fixed at 1 (surfaceWgsl.ts line 399), so nothing near the water occludes or reflects.
findings.fixDirection: Add a short screen-space reflection march in the near-field pass against the depth and colour copies for the reflected ray (a few steps, blurred by the lobe, faded by distance and roughness, falling back to the sky), and use its hit as sky occlusion for the ambient term. Check that the published 'ocean.wetness' wet line is visible on the real capsule material.

findings.defect: The small whitecap specks and the wave texture repeat on a 72.5 m square lattice. At 150 m altitude (0.24 m per px) the autocorrelation has peaks at lags of 300 px in x and y (0.11 in the shaded frame, 0.08 in the foam view, also at 600 px and on the diagonal); shifting the foam view by 300 px makes 574 foam pixels coincide where 38 would by chance.
findings.realReference: No constellation of whitecaps ever repeats; any two 70 m squares of sea are different.
findings.likelyCause: Cascade 2 (patch 8192 / 113 = 72.5 m) contributes foam with weight 0.45 and its waves unmodified (OCEAN_FOAM_WEIGHT, surfaceWgsl.ts line 47; cascades.ts), and the statistical specks have no decorrelation between tiles.
findings.fixDirection: Break the short cascades' foam with a non-periodic term (gate it by the longer cascades' and the long-wave layer's phase, or by the planet-fixed roughness field) and add an autocorrelation bound at the cascade periods to foam.spec.

findings.view: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\ocean\alt10k.png (lower right, x 700-1250, y 470-720); climb-4796m.png; climb-273m.png (far field, y 100-250)
findings.defect: Regular, evenly spaced parallel stripes (corduroy) remain in the resolved water from 300 m to 10 km: autocorrelation peaks 0.14 at lag (17,5) px and 0.11 at (29,11) px in alt10k, 0.09 at (28,4) px in climb-4796m. The review's lattice finding is reduced, not gone.
findings.realReference: Swell seen from altitude is long-crested but irregular: crest spacing and direction wander, lines break and merge.
findings.likelyCause: Four exact sinusoids (data/defs/bodies/earth.json) band-limited by exp(-0.125 (k w)^2) in oceanSwellEval (src/render/ocean/shaders/waves.ts line 121), which still passes 29 % of the amplitude at the pixel Nyquist limit (k w = pi), so the 28 m and 52 m components alias into regular moire once a pixel is 15-25 m.
findings.fixDirection: Steepen the band limit (for example exp(-0.5 (k w)^2), under 1 % at Nyquist) and return the removed variance to the lobe as now; pursue ocean-5 for irregular long waves.

findings.defect: Outside the glitter path the foreground water at sunset is crushed to black: 62 % of pixels are below 8/255 in rows 520-580 and 85-96 % in rows 580-720, while the sky overhead is (67,67,66) and the horizon glow (140,104,31). The lower third of the frame is a black void with a few olive flecks.
findings.realReference: At sunset the near water is dark but readable: slate-blue from the zenith sky on upward-facing facets, orange on the facets tilted toward the glow.
findings.likelyCause: Not isolated. Candidates: the single-tap sky reflection for narrow lobes in waterSkyRadiance (waterBrdf.ts lines 295-313) picks the dark upper sky of the lab's sky-view table for steep view angles and never the horizon glow, since resolved near-field normals leave little lobe width; the body term under a 2.5 deg sun is near zero; the tonemap toe does the rest.
findings.fixDirection: Inspect the skyReflection debug view at this preset and compare it with a mirror-ball render of the same sky; widen the reflection lobe by the true unresolved variance at steep view angles, and check the result under the real atmosphere in the integrated app.

(2) handover-refraction.png is taken in the frame after the ball is switched back on with time frozen, so it shows a TAA ghost of the refracted image and not the converged frame (it lacks the silhouette oval that refraction.png shows). (3) The three refr-diag files are from 19:15 on 10 November, are written by no spec and show rectangular seams at x = 640 and y = 390 that the current build does not have (step at x = 640 under 1/255 in refraction.png and shore.png). Context for this report: the functional specs were re-run through the gate (27 passed, no failure) and the fresh images match the earlier ones to within 4/255 mean; perf-*.png were not regenerated and predate the last ocean commit by 7 minutes.
findings.realReference: Reviewed screenshots show the converged frame of the current build and nothing else; diagnostic overlays show numbers.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/ocean/oceanFeature.ts line 358 (cameraHeight: a?.cameraHeight ?? Number.NaN) printed by labs/ocean/main.ts line 256; tests/browser/ocean/handover.spec.ts lines 104-121 (submerged = true, then saveScreenshot with no wait); leftover files in out/screens/ocean.
findings.fixDirection: Report the camera height when the near field is inactive too, or print 'n/a'; wait for TAA to settle (about 30 frames) before the handover-refraction shot; delete the refr-diag files or produce them from a spec.
